w07q1.intro: Fifteen notices. Some spell the rule out in a whole sentence; some are one word on a wall. Both mean the same thing.

items.prompt: Match each rule to its sign.
items: You cannot bring your dog in here.
You must not make a noise here.
You cannot go through this door.
Please do not walk on the grass.
You must not use your camera here.
items.teach: The first two are yours from the real test — both correct. The pattern generalises.

items.prompt: Match each rule to its sign.
items: It is dangerous to swim here.

items.prompt: Match each rule to its sign.
items: You cannot eat in this room.
Please wait in a line here.
Only people who work here may go in.
We open again at two o'clock.

w07q2.intro: Units 17 and 18 give you the grammar underneath the signs. Can't, shouldn't and must not are three different strengths.

items.prompt: It is against the rules. You ______ run beside the pool.
items.teach: Must not is a rule with teeth. It is the one signs use.

items.prompt: It is not a good idea. You ______ eat sweets all day.
items.teach: Shouldn't is advice. Nobody will stop you; it is simply not wise.

items.prompt: It is impossible. I ______ swim — I never learnt.
items.teach: Can't is about being able to, not about being allowed to.

items.prompt: NO DOGS means…
options: You must not bring a dog.
items.answer: You must not bring a dog.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a rule, not advice?
Build the rule.
items.answer: You must not feed the animals

items.prompt: Build the rule.
items.answer: You can't take photographs in the museum

w07q3.intro: Real signs almost never write the whole sentence. Find the one word that carries it.

items.prompt: “You must not come in.” On a door this is usually just…
“Be careful, the floor is slippery.” On the floor this is usually just…
“Stop your car here.” At a junction this is usually just…
“This shop is not open at the moment.” On the window this is usually just…
items.teach: Back to the shop. One word, and it is the opposite of the word in the sentence.

items.prompt: “You can leave the building through here.” Above the door this is usually just…
“Only people who work here may go past this point.”

boss.intro: A wall of notices, and the Sign Reader wants all of them. Read each one for what it MEANS, not for the place it belongs to.

items.prompt: The shop is not open now.
items.teach: The wall starts with the one that beat you. It does not get to beat you twice.

items.prompt: You cannot bring your dog in here.
You must not make a noise here.
This machine has stopped working.
The last five. Match them all.
items: There are none left to buy.

items.prompt: The café is open every day except Wednesday.
options: It is open only on Wednesday.
